encryption.title: Encrypted Chats
encryption.intro: Chats are end-to-end encrypted, and your phone creates your key automatically. In an encrypted chat, the phone and the server refuse unencrypted messages, and the Aethernet server cannot read the messages. Reporting or translating a message sends that message's text to Aethernet in readable form. In the rare case that someone in a chat has no key, the chat shows Not encrypted, and its messages are stored readable on our server.
encryption.notSignedIn: Sign in to your Aethernet account first.
encryption.unsupportedBody: This computer cannot create the security key that encrypted chats need. This usually happens when the game runs through Wine or Proton. If your account has no key yet, your chats still work here but are not encrypted. Chats encrypted with a key from another computer cannot be read or sent from here. The rest of Aetherphone works normally.
encryption.unsupportedSummary: This PC cannot set up encryption, so messages here are not encrypted.
encryption.activeHint: Encryption is active on this device. It works automatically. There is nothing to set up.
encryption.newDeviceHint: On another computer this account starts locked. Your recovery code, or approval from a computer that already has your key, unlocks it there with your full history.
encryption.localStoreUnavailable: This PC can't use the system's secure key store, so your encryption key is saved with basic protection instead. Your chats keep working normally on this device.
encryption.lockedBody: This device doesn't have the encryption key for this account, so messages here can't be read yet. This usually happens after switching to a different computer. Your messages are safe: open Aetherphone on the computer that already has your key, or create a new key here. If you create a new key, older messages become readable again once your chat partners come online.
encryption.newKeyButton: Create a new key on this device…
encryption.lockedNoRecoveryBody: This device doesn't hold an encryption key for this account, and no recovery code was set up, so the old key can't be restored here. Create a new key anyway: everyone you talk to still holds the key to the chats you share, and their phone hands it to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone. Only a chat where everyone lost their key stays closed.
encryption.forgotNoRecoveryBody: A new key will be created. The key it replaces stays on this PC, so older messages keep opening here, and the people you chat with hand the key to your shared chats back to the new one when they next open Aetherphone. Save a recovery code afterwards so this PC is never the only way in.
encryption.lockedRecoverBody: This device doesn't have your encryption key yet. Enter the recovery code you saved to restore your chats here, with your full history.
encryption.lockedBanner: Chats are locked on this device. Tap to unlock.
encryption.recoveryNudgeBanner: Protect your chat history: set up a recovery code
encryption.recoveryNotSetBody: Set up a recovery code so you can restore your chats if you reinstall or move to another PC. Without one, a new PC depends on your other PC or the people you chat with to unlock older chats.
encryption.recoveryConfiguredBody: A recovery code is set up for this account. Keep it somewhere safe: it's what unlocks your chats on another PC.
encryption.recoverySaveBody: This code restores your chats on another PC without help from another device or the people you chat with, and it can't be shown again. Keep it somewhere safe and private: anyone with this code can read your chats.
encryption.recoveryWrongCode: That code didn't work. Check it and try again.
encryption.recoveryOlderCode: That code is from before your key changed, so it can't unlock current chats, but the older chats it protects were unlocked on this PC. To unlock everything, use your newest code, your other PC, or create a new key.
encryption.recoveryKeyChanged: Your encryption key changed on another device, so this device can't create a recovery code right now. Wait a moment for this device to update, then try again.
encryption.restoreOlderBody: Keys replaced on this PC are tried automatically, and the people you chat with hand their copy of the conversation key back to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone. Messages sealed to a key that was never here can also be unlocked with the recovery code you had at the time.
encryption.olderKeysHeldHere: Older keys kept on this PC: {0}
encryption.restoreOlderDone: Keys restored: {0}. Older messages are now readable on this device.
encryption.restoreOlderNoMatch: That code didn't match any older keys.
encryption.restoreOlderRetry: Your chats are unlocked, but checking for older keys failed. Open Older chats and enter the same code to try again.
encryption.forgotBody: A new key will be created. The key it replaces stays on this PC, so older messages keep opening here, and the people you chat with hand the key to your shared chats back to the new one when they next open Aetherphone. Keep your current recovery code: it is what opens your older messages on another PC.
encryption.olderKeyBanner: Some messages here were sent to an earlier key. They unlock when the other person next opens Aetherphone. Tap for details.
encryption.linkBody: If Aetherphone still works on your other computer, it can unlock this one for you. No code to type, and your full history comes with it.
encryption.linkWaitingBody: Open Aetherphone on your other computer and approve this request. Check that it shows the same number.
encryption.linkApproveBody: Another computer signed in to your account is asking to open your chats. Only approve this if it is you, and only if that computer shows the same number: {0}
encryption.guideSaveBody: Your chats are encrypted. Save the code that unlocks them on another PC.
encryption.guideLockedBody: This PC does not hold your encryption key yet. Open Encrypted Chats to unlock it.
encryption.guideVerifyBody: Type the last group of your code to confirm you saved it correctly.
encryption.guideVerifyWrong: That does not match the last group. Check your code and try again.
encryption.summaryNoRecovery: No recovery code, chats cannot move to another PC
encryption.helpOpen: What to do if chats stop opening
encryption.helpIntro: Losing the key on this PC does not delete your messages from the server, so almost every case below is fixable.
encryption.helpDecryptingBody: Nothing is wrong. The keys for that chat are still loading and the messages appear within a few seconds. If it stays like this, reopen the phone.
encryption.helpLockedTitle: It says Locked on this device
encryption.helpLockedBody: This PC does not hold your key. If your other computer still works, use Unlock from my other PC above and approve it there: that is instant and brings everything. Otherwise enter your recovery code. If you have neither, create a new key: the people you chat with hand the key to your shared conversations back to it when they next open Aetherphone, and those chats open again.
encryption.helpOlderKeyTitle: It says Sent to an earlier key
encryption.helpOlderKeyBody: Those messages were written before your key changed. Keys replaced on this PC are tried automatically, and everyone you chat with still holds the conversation key: their phone hands it back to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone, so most of these clear on their own with nothing for you to do. A chat that stays locked means that person has not been online since your key changed, or lost their own key too. The recovery code you had at the time still opens it: see Older chats below.
encryption.helpUnreadableTitle: Windows will not open the key
encryption.helpUnreadableBody: The key is still saved here, Windows just refuses to open it. This happens when the game runs as a different Windows user, as administrator when it usually is not, or after Windows was reinstalled. Start the game the way you normally do and it should unlock itself.
encryption.helpDamagedTitle: It says This message is damaged
encryption.helpDamagedBody: That single message did not arrive intact. It cannot be repaired, but it does not affect the rest of the chat or your key.
encryption.helpNeverBody: Unlocking from another PC is the best route: it is instant and brings everything back. A recovery code is next. A new key comes last, but it is no longer a dead end: this PC keeps the key it replaces, and everyone you chat with hands back the key to each conversation you share once they open Aetherphone again. The one thing a new key cannot bring back is a chat where every other person lost their key too.
encryption.helpPreventBody: Keep a recovery code saved, and keep every code you have ever generated: each one opens only the key it was made for. This PC also holds on to the keys it replaces, the people you chat with hand their copy of a shared conversation key back to whatever key you have now, and messages you have already read stay readable even if the key is lost. A code is still worth keeping: it is what works when nobody else is around to hand a key back.
encryption.lockedNoRecoveryBanner: Your old chats can't be opened on this PC yet. Tap to fix it.
encryption.unreadableKeyBody: Windows could not open the encryption key saved on this PC. This usually means the game is running as a different Windows user, or Windows was reinstalled. Your key is still here and untouched: start the game the way you normally do and it should unlock. Try that before creating a new key, since nothing has actually been lost.
encryption.saveCodeBanner: Save your recovery code so you never lose these chats
encryption.saveCodeIntro: Encryption is set up on this device. Save this code now: it opens your chats on another PC, or on this one after a reset, without help from another device or the people you chat with.
encryption.composerBlocked: This chat is encrypted and this device can't open its key. Tap to fix.
encryption.reportDisclosure: This message and up to 5 previous messages, including photos and voice notes, will be shared with the moderators, decrypted.
encryption.waitingMembers: {0} can't receive encrypted messages yet. Messages stay unencrypted until everyone has an encryption key.
encryption.securityCodeHint: Compare this code with {0}. If both phones show the same code, this chat is end-to-end encrypted.
encryption.securityCodeUnavailable: The security code appears once both of you have encryption keys.
report.summarySpam: Repeated posts, unwanted ads, phishing or malicious links, or selling gil, accounts or services for real money.
report.summaryHarassment: Attacking, accusing or humiliating a specific player, or contacting them after they asked you to stop.
report.summaryHate: A slur, or dehumanising or excluding language about race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability or illness.
report.summaryThreats: Threats or wishes of real-world harm against a person or group, or encouraging violence against them.
report.summaryExplicit: Nudity, sexual acts or language, fetish content, or asking for or offering erotic roleplay.
report.summaryVelvetProhibited: A prohibited fetish, sexualized violence, extreme gore, or anything else the Velvet rules forbid.
report.summaryConsent: Unsolicited explicit content, pressure into roleplay, or continuing after a refusal or a stated limit.
report.summaryInGame: Real-life photos, posts unrelated to the game, or real-world political content.
report.summaryCreators: Reposting someone's art or screenshots without permission, removing credit, or images made or altered by AI.
report.summaryImpersonation: Pretending to be another player, a moderator, a developer, or a venue or community.
report.summaryPrivacy: Sharing someone's real-world identity, or screenshots of tells, party, linkshell or direct messages.
report.summarySelfHarm: Encouraging, instructing or glorifying self-harm, suicide or eating disorders.
report.summaryChildSafety: Sexualizing a minor or a character with a child-like appearance, whatever the stated age.
report.summaryExploitation: Sexual exploitation, intimate images shared without consent, deepfakes of real people, or blackmail.
report.summaryEvasion: A new or alternate account used to get around a suspension or a block.
report.summaryOther: Anything else that breaks the community rules.
report.sent: Thank you for your report. Our moderation team will review it, and we may take action if it violates our Community Guidelines.

games.tetris.hook: Rotate and drop the falling pieces to fill whole lines and clear them.
games.2048.hook: Slide the tiles to merge matching numbers and build your way up to 2048.
games.minesweeper.hook: Reveal every safe square and flag the mines before one goes off.
games.memory.hook: Flip two cards at a time and match every pair in as few tries as you can.
games.match3.hook: Swap neighboring gems to line up three or more and keep the cascades coming.
games.breakout.hook: Bounce the ball off your paddle to smash every brick without letting it drop.
games.bubbles.hook: Aim and shoot bubbles into groups of three or more to pop them before they reach the line.
games.watersort.hook: Pour the liquids between tubes until every tube holds a single color.
games.coinTimerHint: Aether Coin timer: stay in this game until the countdown ends to earn coins. It keeps counting while the game is paused.
games.coinTimerDeepHint: Coins earned. Stay in this game until the countdown ends for the long session bonus. It keeps counting while the game is paused.
games.coinTimerDoneHint: Coins earned for this game, including the long session bonus.
games.coinTimerCooldownHint: Aether Coin timer starts soon: a new timer can begin one minute after the last one started. Stay in this game and it starts on its own.
games.nonogram.hook: Use the number clues to fill the right cells and reveal the hidden picture.
games.flow.hook: Connect each pair of matching dots with pipes that fill the whole grid without crossing.
games.solitaire.hook: Build the four foundations from ace to king by moving cards between the columns.
games.simon.hook: Watch the pads light up, then repeat the sequence back without a mistake.
games.flap.hook: Tap to flap through the gaps in the pipes and see how far you can fly.
games.reversi.hook: Outflank the CPU's discs to flip them and own the most of the board when it fills.
games.whack.hook: Tap the moles before they hide. Bombs cost you points.
games.snake.hook: Steer the snake to the fruit and never touch yourself.
games.sudoku.hook: Fill the grid so every row, column and box holds the digits one to nine.
games.chess.hook: Checkmate the CPU's king and keep your win streak alive.
games.stack.hook: Drop each slab on the one below; anything that hangs over gets cut away.
games.crystaldrop.hook: Drop crystals into the jar and merge matching ones before it overflows.
games.beat.hook: Hit each note as it reaches the line and keep the combo going.
games.blade.hook: Throw your blades into the spinning wheel without hitting one already stuck there.
games.trivia.hook: Look at the icon and pick the right name before the timer runs out.
games.skyfall.hook: Fire at the falling missiles before they reach your cities.
games.invaders.hook: Slide left and right and shoot down the alien waves before they land.
games.capman.hook: Eat every pellet in the maze while dodging the ghosts, or grab a power pellet and chase them.
games.hop.hook: Hop across the road and the river, one lane at a time, without getting hit or swept away.
games.squadron.hook: Weave through the enemy formations and shoot them down stage after stage.
games.doom.hook: Fight your way through the demons on Mars with WASD, the mouse and Space.

games.wordrun.hook: Guess the five-letter word in six tries; the colors tell you which letters are right.
